outcome: The problem (determining the true order of the error term Δ_k(x) in the generalized/Piltz divisor problem) remains open for every k≥2, but several explicit-constant and exponent improvements were published within the window, most concretely Sebastian Tudzi's paper giving explicit numerical bounds |Δ₃(x)| < 2.968x^(2/3)log^(1/3)x and general-k bounds with explicit constants for k=4,5,6, first posted to arXiv 26 June 2025 and later published in the Ramanujan Journal (2026). No AI system was involved in any of the papers examined.
summary: The Piltz (generalized Dirichlet) divisor problem asks for the true order of Δ_k(x) = D_k(x) − xP_k(log x), the error term when d_k(n) (n written as a product of k factors) is summed up to x; for every k this remains open, since only upper bounds on the exponent α_k are known and the conjectured optimal value α_k = 1/2 − 1/(2k) has not been proven for any k≥2. Within the window (26 Jan 2024 to present) I found no resolution of the problem for any k, but several genuine incremental results narrowing/explicating known bounds. The clearest is Sebastian Tudzi, 'On the Generalised Divisor Problem' (arXiv:2506.21823, posted 26 June 2025, published in Ramanujan J. 70 (2026)), which via the Dirichlet convolution method gives an explicit numerical bound |Δ₃(x)| < 2.968·x^(2/3)(log x)^(1/3) for all x≥2 (improving prior explicit constants for k=3) and explicit constants for the general-k bound Δ_k(x) = O(x^((k-1)/k)(log x)^((k-1)(k-2)/(2k))) for k=4,5,6 with a recurrence for larger k. I read the arXiv HTML full text including the acknowledgements section, which thanks the author's supervisor Timothy S. Trudgian and several colleagues for discussion — no computational or AI tool is mentioned anywhere. I also checked two other leads the triage pass surfaced: (1) Minamide, Tanigawa and Watt, 'On the sum of Δ_k(n) in the Piltz divisor problem for k=3 and k=4' (arXiv:2412.11069, posted 15 Dec 2024, published Acta Arithmetica 216.4 (2024)) — this bounds the *summed* quantity Σ_{n≤x}Δ_k(n), a related but distinct object from Δ_k(x) itself; I judged this a case/adjacent result worth noting but it does not itself move the bound on Δ_k(x) as stated in the bullet, and its abstract shows no AI involvement. (2) A preprints.org manuscript ('On the Generalized Dirichlet Divisor Problem', May 2025) claimed by triage to give improved α_k bounds for 9≤k≤20 — this page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch and I could not read it directly; Tao's expdb blueprint (teorth.github.io) corroborates that a 2025 result by 'Li' improves α_k for k in the 9–20 range (its Theorem 16.20), competing with earlier Trudgian–Yang bounds (Theorem 16.19, from arXiv:2306.05599, whose v1 predates the window (9 June 2023) but whose v3 was posted 15 July 2024, inside the window — I could not confirm from the abstract alone whether v3 added genuinely new results or was a revision of the same June-2023 result, so I am not resting the status on it). I also checked and ruled out two other candidate events as predating the window: Bellotti–Yang's large-k bound Δ_k(x) ≪ x^(1−1.889k^(−2/3)) (arXiv:2303.05028, posted 9 March 2023, journal-published in BLMS May 2024 — the journal date is not the event date per §6.3) and Li–Yang's α₂ ≤ 0.314483... (arXiv:2308.14859, posted 28 August 2023). Both predate 26 January 2024 and would be open_stale if they were the only evidence, but since the Tudzi 2025 result is a genuine in-window improvement, the overall status is 'progress' rather than 'open_stale'. I found no trace of AI/LLM involvement anywhere in this corner of analytic number theory: no papers, blog posts, or lab announcements connect the Piltz/generalized divisor problem to any AI system. This is consistent with the nature of the problem — it requires exponential-sum and zeta-moment estimation techniques that are far from current AI theorem-proving benchmarks (IMO-style problems, short combinatorial arguments), and no lab or Lean/AI project appears to have targeted it.
competing_reading: One could argue the Tudzi paper's contribution is narrow enough (explicit constants for an already-known asymptotic exponent, not a new exponent) that it should be 'open' rather than 'progress' — the qualitative bound O(x^((k-1)/k)(log x)^(...)) for k≥4 was already the known form; what changed is the numerical constant λ_k. I classified it as 'progress' because bounding constants explicitly is itself the kind of incremental movement the triage/audit rules treat as counting (§3.1: 'a bound that moved a little... counts'), and because the k=3 case did tighten the known exponent-adjacent estimate with an explicit, checkable numerical inequality. A stricter reading limiting 'progress' to exponent (not just constant) improvements would instead call this 'open' with the Tudzi paper noted as a near-miss.
what_would_settle_it: Reading the preprints.org manuscript directly (currently blocked by a 403) to see exactly which α_k values for 9≤k≤20 it improves and whether it substantively differs from the Trudgian–Yang and Li results already logged in Tao's expdb; and diffing arXiv:2306.05599 v1 (June 2023) against v3 (July 2024) to see whether the divisor-problem-relevant theorem was added or only revised in the window.
